Battery safety
A LiPo is safe when you treat it right. When it goes wrong, it goes wrong fast.
Takeaway
At the first sign: get it out, or get out. Fast.
Free to use in your own trainings. Just tell people where you got it.
HOBIZONE.ORG
15 · Battery safety · fig. 1
What makes a LiPo burn
A LiPo has no protection circuit. Almost every fire starts with one of these.
1
Crash damage
A hit can crush a cell inside. It may look fine and fail later.
2
Overcharging
Wrong chemistry, wrong cell count or a broken charger.
3
Short circuit
Bare leads touching, a screw through the pack, a cut wire.
4
Puffed packs
Gas inside means the pack is damaged. It only gets worse.
5
Heat
A hot car, direct sun, charging a pack that is still hot from flying.
6
Emptying it too far
Below 3.0 V per cell the cells get damaged, and a damaged cell is risky to charge.
Free to use in your own trainings. Just tell people where you got it.
HOBIZONE.ORG
15 · Battery safety · fig. 2
Puffed or damaged? Retire it
A pack doesn’t heal. If in doubt, it’s done.
puffed: soft, round, swollen
1
Signs
Swollen or soft, dented or cut, hot after a gentle flight, a cell that drops much faster than the others.
2
Don’t
Don’t charge it, don’t fly it, don’t press it flat, don’t puncture it.
3
Do
Put it in a LiPo bag or a metal box, away from anything that burns. Then dispose of it.
Free to use in your own trainings. Just tell people where you got it.
HOBIZONE.ORG
15 · Battery safety · fig. 3
How a LiPo fire goes
From first warning to flames can be about 10 seconds. After a crash, there may be no warning at all.
1 · Puff
The pack swells. Gas is building up inside.
2 · Hiss
Gas and smoke vent out. Flames often follow within seconds.
3 · Fire
Jets of flame. One cell lights the next, every 10 to 15 s.
4 · Sleeping dragon
Looks out, but it can flare up again hours later.
pssss…
zzz…
Free to use in your own trainings. Just tell people where you got it.
HOBIZONE.ORG
15 · Battery safety · fig. 4
Know the smell
The smell is often the first warning, before you see anything. Learn it.
Sickeningly sweet. Like strong flowers or cheap air freshener.
That smell has no place in a technical area. If you smell it, find the source now.
1
Don’t breathe it
The smoke is toxic. It can contain hydrogen fluoride.
2
Not always
Some of the gas has no smell, so no smell doesn’t mean all clear.
3
Sound too
Hissing, popping, crackling from a pack: same message.
Free to use in your own trainings. Just tell people where you got it.
HOBIZONE.ORG
15 · Battery safety · fig. 5
Seconds, and a bigger flame than you think
When it goes, you have seconds, not minutes. Don’t try to save the pack.
4–5 m in our tests
1
A jet, not a candle
Flames shoot sideways and up, metres from the pack.
2
Fast
About 10 s from smoke to flame. A whole pack in a minute or two.
3
Toxic smoke
It fills a room in moments. Get out and close the door.
Free to use in your own trainings. Just tell people where you got it.
HOBIZONE.ORG
15 · Battery safety · fig. 6
Where to charge
Charge as if it will catch fire. Clear the whole area, not just the desk.
1
Fireproof surface
Stone, tiles, metal or a ceramic tile. Never a bed, carpet or wooden desk.
2
Clear around it
Nothing that burns within several metres: curtains, paper, boxes, other packs.
3
LiPo bag or box
It holds the flames in for a while. It doesn’t put the fire out.
4
Never unattended
Stay in the room. Don’t charge overnight or while you’re out.
5
Smoke detector
In the room where you charge, and know where the exit is.
6
Cool pack, cool room
Let a pack cool after flying. Never charge below 0 °C or in the sun.
Free to use in your own trainings. Just tell people where you got it.
HOBIZONE.ORG
15 · Battery safety · fig. 7
If it catches fire
Kids: shout for an adult, get out, stay out. Adults:
1
Unplug at the wall
Not by grabbing the battery.
2
Get out, close the door
If it’s already burning indoors. Call 112.
3
Lots of water
Water is right for a LiPo: it cools it. Powder and CO₂ don’t.
4
Into a bucket outside
When it stops hissing: tongs or a shovel, into water. Sand doesn’t cool.
5
Leave it a day
It can flare up hours later. 24 h in water, then the jäätmejaam.
More in the talk “Safety”.
Free to use in your own trainings. Just tell people where you got it.
HOBIZONE.ORG
15 · Battery safety · fig. 8
Storing your packs
A stored pack can still burn. Store it so that a fire stays small.
1
3.8 V per cell
Use the charger’s storage mode if you won’t fly in a day or two.
2
Fireproof box
A metal ammo box (with the seal removed) or a LiPo bag, not a drawer.
3
Cool and dry
Room temperature or a bit cooler. Not in a car, not in the sun.
Free to use in your own trainings. Just tell people where you got it.
HOBIZONE.ORG
15 · Battery safety · fig. 9
Getting rid of a pack
Never in the household rubbish. In a bin truck, a crushed LiPo starts fires.
1
Empty it
Discharge it slowly with the charger, as low as it lets you.
2
Tape the leads
Tape over the connector so the wires can’t touch.
3
Take it back
To a jäätmejaam, or a battery box in a shop that sells batteries. It’s free.
4
Puffed or hot?
Keep it in a metal box or bucket of sand outside until you take it.
Free to use in your own trainings. Just tell people where you got it.

15 · Battery safety · fig. 10
Flying with LiPos
Going to a race abroad? Spare LiPos travel in your hand luggage only.
Pack size
Rule
up to 100 Wh
Allowed in hand luggage, no approval
100–160 Wh
Airline approval, at most 2
over 160 Wh
Not allowed
Each pack in a LiPo bag or its own pouch, leads taped.
Fly with packs at storage voltage or lower. Some airlines ask for 25 % or less.
Check your airline’s rules before every trip. They change.
A 6S 1300 mAh pack is 28.9 Wh: fine. Some airlines still limit how many spares you can bring.
Free to use in your own trainings. Just tell people where you got it.

Remember
At the first sign: get it out, or get out. Fast.
1
Know the smell: sickeningly sweet, like cheap air freshener.
2
Puff, hiss, fire: about 10 seconds. After a crash, no warning.
3
The flame is much bigger than you think. Clear the whole area.
4
Never charge unattended, on a bed, or below 0 °C.
5
Puffed or damaged: retire it. Never in the household rubbish.
6
Water is right for a LiPo fire. Then 24 h in a bucket outside.
Free to use in your own trainings. Just tell people where you got it.
